paper.title: Algorithm 832: UMFPACK V4.3 -- an unsymmetric-pattern multifrontal method
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 30(2), June 2004, p. 196 (per the frame item); article not fetched

field: numerics (sparse LU factorization, multifrontal method, fill-reducing ordering)
stack: C (UMFPACK V4.3 with AMD V1.1, netlib CALGO 832.zip, stock Make/Make.include: CONFIG = -DNBLAS, CFLAGS = -O; gcc 13.3.0 from Ubuntu 24.04; the Fortran readhb helpers built with gfortran 16.2.0 from conda-forge)

claim.text: The 'numeric factorization flops' value printed for the west0067 matrix (HB/west0067.rua, 67 by 67, 294 entries) by the shipped reference output UMFPACK/Demo/umf4.out, 1.41920e+04, agrees with the value the rerun prints for the same matrix within absolute tolerance 0.05 (registered before any run; the claim is the code's own shipped reference output, not a value from the paper).
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed input HB/west0067.rua; AMD and COLAMD orderings with fixed defaults, no random numbers)

attempt: G1 original attempt: the authors' tree as shipped, with its stock Make/Make.include, run as 'make hb' in UMFPACK/Demo, builds UMFPACK, AMD and umf4 and then fails at readhb: 'make: f77: No such file or directory' (no Fortran compiler named f77 in the sandbox). Patch (build-only, no source file touched): gfortran 16.2.0 from conda-forge installed in the sandbox during the fetch step, and the same 'make hb' run with the command-line variable F77=gfortran. The west0067 run then gives the flop line 'numeric factorization flops 1.41920e+04', identical to the shipped reference at its printed precision, in two clean passes.

original_attempt.reason: stock make hb cannot build the Fortran readhb helpers: the stock Make.include names the Fortran compiler f77, which the sandbox does not have (make: f77: No such file or directory, exit 2)
